\section*{Limitations}

Our study has several limitations.
First, our primary experiments use a single dataset (591 problems from HumanEval and MBPP-sanitized); while a cross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench (\S\ref{sec:debugbench}) confirms that exception dominance generalizes to synthetically injected bugs, generalization to other languages, larger codebases, or real-world fault distributions remains untested.
Second, while we evaluate four models spanning 1.5B to 13B parameters across three architecture families, all are code-specialized; generalization to general-purpose models or larger scales remains untested.
Third, DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} exhibits seed-dependent variance: 2/3 seeds achieve 99.33\% while seed 123 yields 91.09\% ($\sigma{=}4.76$pp, $n{=}3$), which we hypothesize reflects LoRA initialization sensitivity in DeepSeek-Coder, though direct evidence is lacking (fail recall = 70.5\% for the outlier vs.\ 100\% for others).
Qwen \texttt{exception\_only} shows perfect seed robustness ($\sigma{=}0$, $n{=}3$), but Qwen \texttt{ae\_only} also exhibits seed variance ($\sigma{=}$0.40pp; seed 123 = 99.08\% vs.\ seeds 42/456 = 99.92\%), though far smaller than DeepSeek's ($\sigma{=}$4.76pp).
Whether training stabilization techniques can eliminate DeepSeek's seed sensitivity is unexplored; other conditions use a single seed.
Fourth, the initial DeepSeek \texttt{full\_trace} run was invalidated by context overflow; a re-run with extended context yields 79.16\% (CI [76.80\%, 81.30\%]), 2.60pp below Qwen (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}).
Fifth, the candidate solutions were generated by Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, which also serves as one of our evaluation models; this does not affect verdict prediction but may influence the pass/fail distribution.
Sixth, self-familiarity bias may inflate absolute accuracy: both Qwen-2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder were likely exposed to HumanEval and MBPP solutions during pretraining, so the models may partially recognize solutions rather than purely reasoning from trace signals; our cross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench mitigates but does not eliminate this concern.
Seventh, the error distribution in our test set may not reflect real-world fault distributions: exceptions (especially \texttt{TypeError}, \texttt{ValueError}) dominate LLM-generated failures, but production code may exhibit a broader spectrum of silent logic errors where no exception is raised, potentially reducing the effectiveness of exception-based verdict prediction.
Finally, our analysis is limited to verdict prediction; whether the information density advantage extends to other trace-based tasks is an open question.

\section*{Ethics Statement}

This work uses publicly available benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP-sanitized, DebugBench) and does not involve human subjects, crowdsourced annotations, or personally identifiable information.
All models evaluated are open-source and publicly accessible.
Training uses parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with each experiment using a single GPU.
Total compute is approximately 320 GPU-hours across all conditions, models, seeds, and iterative refinements (including approximately 170 hours for successful experiments; individual runs range from 0.5h for small models to 2.2h for CodeLlama-13B, with the total reflecting 4 models $\times$ multiple conditions $\times$ multiple seeds $\times$ iterative development).

20	# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）
21	
22	> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
23	> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）
28	
29	### 1.1 数字必须有源头
30	
31	- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
32	- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
33	- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
34	- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance
35	
36	> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。
37	
38	### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用
39	
40	- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol
41	- 两张表如果 protocol 不同（如 0-shot vs 8-shot），论文必须明确说明
42	- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
43	- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）
44	
45	> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。
46	
47	### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活
48	
49	- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
50	- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
51	- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配
56	
57	### 2.1 Claim 强度规则
58	
59	| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
60	|----------|--------------|
61	| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
62	| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
63	| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
64	| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
65	| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
66	| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |
67	
68	### 2.2 禁止的过强表述
69	
70	- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
71	- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
72	- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
73	- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
74	- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
75	- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"
76	
77	### 2.3 Claim 降级机制
78	
79	当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
80	- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
81	- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
82	- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix
83	
84	---

88	### 3.1 结构原则
89	
90	- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
91	- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
92	- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
93	- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
94	- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组
95	
96	### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）
97	
98	- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
99	- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名
100	
101	### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字
102	
103	新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。
104	
105	### 3.4 Contingency Plan
106	
107	关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。

109	### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策
110

125	- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
126	- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步
127	
128	### 4.3 p-value 格式
129	
130	- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
131	- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明
132

134	
135	Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。

# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）

> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。

---

## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）

### 1.1 数字必须有源头

- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance

> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。

### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用

- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol
- 两张表如果 protocol 不同（如 0-shot vs 8-shot），论文必须明确说明
- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）

> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。

### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活

- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）

---

## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配

### 2.1 Claim 强度规则

| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
|----------|--------------|
| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |

### 2.2 禁止的过强表述

- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"

### 2.3 Claim 降级机制

当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix

---

## 三、叙事与 Storytelling

### 3.1 结构原则

- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组

### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）

- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名

### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字

新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。

### 3.4 Contingency Plan

关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。

### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策

70% 进度时的估计往往不够稳定（尤其 GSM8K 等难度分布不均匀的 benchmark），必须等完整数据再定稿叙事。

---

## 四、术语与一致性

### 4.1 术语一致性

- 全文必须统一使用正式定义的术语，不得出现同义词漂移
- 术语定义后，每次使用必须完全一致（不要有时 "perturbation sensitivity" 有时 "perturbation impact"）

### 4.2 统计量一致性

- 两个不同的 kappa/p-value 每次出现时必须标注是哪个
- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步

### 4.3 p-value 格式

- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明

### 4.4 例子与定义必须一致

Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。

---

## 五、投稿前检查清单（Pre-Submission Checklist）

### 5.1 占位符扫描（硬门禁）

提交前必须 grep 扫描，以下模式要求**零匹配**：
```
XX.XX, PLACEHOLDER, [If , TODO, TBD, \placeholder{
```
所有条件占位段落（`[If ...]`）必须替换为最终文本。

### 5.2 编译检查

- [ ] 编译零 error
- [ ] 无 `??` 未解析引用
- [ ] 无 > 1pt 的 overfull hbox
- [ ] 正文 ≤ 9 页（NeurIPS desk reject 风险）
- [ ] 使用当年 style file（`neurips_2026.sty`）
- [ ] Review 版启用行号
- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢

### 5.3 数据完整性

- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明

### 5.4 图表检查

- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）

- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐

### 5.6 匿名化检查

- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露

### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）

- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）

### 5.8 叙事完整性

- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）

### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查

- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段

### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对

- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐

\section{Experiments}

We evaluate across two research questions:
(1)~Do Tier~1 exception signals generalize across models?
(2)~What is the relative contribution of each trace component?
All experiments use $N{=}1{,}190$ test samples; accuracy is reported with Wilson 95\% CIs.\footnote{Data is partitioned at the problem level (472 train / 119 test problems, zero crossover; \S\ref{sec:dataset}). The \texttt{exception\_only} format collapses passing solutions into identical rows (48.99\% test duplicates; Appendix~\ref{sec:dedup_stats}), but these arise from within-problem variants, not cross-set leakage; deduplication sensitivity analysis confirms 0.00pp delta across all 19 experimental conditions.}
Pairwise comparisons use paired bootstrap resampling ($B{=}10{,}000$, seed=42); all differences are significant at $p{<}0.0001$ unless noted.

\subsection{Cross-Model Comparison}
\label{sec:cross_model}

Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} compares four models spanning an 8.7$\times$ parameter range (1.5B--13B) and three architecture families (Qwen, DeepSeek, CodeLlama) under key conditions.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Cross-model verdict accuracy (\%, $N{=}1{,}190$) across four models (1.5B--13B) and three architecture families. Multi-seed entries report mean$\pm$std over 3 seeds. Bold: best per model. Full per-seed breakdowns in Appendix~\ref{sec:full_results}; per-class metrics in Appendix~\ref{sec:per_class}.}
\label{tab:cross_model}
\small
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Qwen-7B} & \textbf{Qwen-1.5B} & \textbf{CL-13B} & \textbf{DS-6.7B} \\
\midrule
exception\_only & \textbf{99.83}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.00} & \textbf{99.83}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.00} & \textbf{99.89}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.10} & \textbf{99.33}$^\dag$ \\
ae\_only & 99.64{\scriptsize$\pm$0.49} & --- & --- & 98.74 \\
VOTA & 99.05{\scriptsize$\pm$0.38} & 99.58 & 98.57 & 99.25$^\ddag$ \\
loop\_only & 86.05{\scriptsize$\pm$0.52} & --- & 77.06 & 81.26 \\
no\_trace & 75.13 & 67.31 & 76.47 & 73.36 \\
\midrule
Majority baseline & \multicolumn{4}{c}{71.51} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}%
}
\vspace{2pt}
\par\raggedright\footnotesize
$^\dag$DeepSeek 3-seed mean 96.58\%$\pm$4.76pp; seed 123 (91.09\%, fail recall\,=\,70.5\%) exhibits format collapse on long inputs (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}), reported as 2-seed mean excluding the outlier.
VOTA on Qwen-7B: 99.41/98.66/99.08 ($\sigma{=}$0.38).
\texttt{ae\_only} 3 seeds: 99.92/99.08/99.92 (mean 99.64\%); Qwen-7B \texttt{loop\_only} 3 seeds: 85.63/85.88/86.64 (mean 86.05\%).
Qwen-1.5B \texttt{exception\_only}: 99.83\% across 3 seeds ($\sigma{=}$0).
$^\ddag$DeepSeek VOTA 3 seeds: 84.45/99.16/99.33; seed 42 (84.45\%, fail recall\,=\,45.4\%) is a training failure due to tokenizer-driven truncation (Appendix~\ref{sec:tokenizer_analysis}), reported as 2-seed mean.
\end{table}

\paragraph{Exception dominance across families.}
Under \texttt{exception\_only}, the Qwen and CodeLlama families achieve ${\geq}$99.83\% (mean): Qwen-7B (99.83\%$\pm$0.00, 3 seeds), Qwen-1.5B (99.83\%), and CodeLlama-13B (99.89\%$\pm$0.10, 3 seeds; seed 123 achieves 100\%).
DeepSeek-6.7B reaches 99.33\% on 2/3 seeds with one LoRA-sensitivity outlier at 91.09\% (seed 123; fail recall = 70.5\%).
Excluding the DeepSeek outlier, the cross-model range is 0.56pp (99.33--99.89\%), the tightest of any condition.

\paragraph{Scale invariance of exception signals.}
Exception-based accuracy is shared by models spanning 1.5B to 13B parameters (8.7$\times$): both Qwen-1.5B and CodeLlama-13B achieve 99.83\%+ on the same representation.
CodeLlama-13B seed 123 achieves 100\% (0/1190 errors), confirming that Qwen's two persistent errors (from \texttt{GeneratorExit}; Appendix~\ref{sec:irreducible}) are high-probability convergence artifacts rather than hard data limitations.
In contrast, \texttt{no\_trace} scales monotonically with capacity: 67.31\% (1.5B) $\to$ 75.13\% (7B) $\to$ 76.47\% (13B), a 9.16pp range that exception events completely eliminate (Figure~\ref{fig:cross_scale}).

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig3_cross_model_gap}
\caption{Verdict accuracy vs.\ model scale. \texttt{exception\_only} maintains ${\geq}$99.33\% regardless of scale (1.5B--13B), while \texttt{no\_trace} shows monotonic scale sensitivity (+9.16pp from 1.5B to 13B). The \texttt{nomarker} condition (format markers removed) shows no degradation at smaller scale (${\sim}$97.7--97.8\%).}
\label{fig:cross_scale}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{VOTA cross-family variation.}
Excluding outlier seeds, VOTA achieves ${\geq}$98.57\% across all four models: 99.58\% (Qwen-1.5B) $>$ 99.25\%$\pm$0.12 (DeepSeek-6.7B, 2 seeds) $>$ 99.05\%$\pm$0.38 (Qwen-7B, 3 seeds) $>$ 98.57\% (CodeLlama-13B; CI [97.9, 99.2]), a 1.01pp range.
DeepSeek seed 42 (84.45\%, fail recall = 45.4\%) is a training failure driven by tokenizer-induced truncation (91.7\% of training samples affected; Appendix~\ref{sec:tokenizer_analysis}); the remaining seeds (99.16\%, 99.33\%) match cross-model performance.
\texttt{exception\_only} inputs are compact (median 150 tokens), sidestepping truncation entirely (Appendix~\ref{sec:robustness_analysis}).

\subsection{Component Ablation}
\label{sec:ablation}

Multi-seed \texttt{ae\_only} ablations use Qwen-7B; \texttt{loop\_only} is evaluated across three models to test Tier~2 generalization (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}).
Table~\ref{tab:ablation} decomposes VOTA on Qwen-2.5-7B and reveals a two-tier hierarchy: Tier~1 (\texttt{exception\_only}) generalizes across all four models (${\geq}$99.33\%), while Tier~2 (\texttt{loop\_only}) is model-dependent.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Component ablation on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$). Tier~1 signals achieve near-perfect accuracy; combining them (VOTA) slightly dilutes performance. $^\dag$\texttt{ae\_only}: 3-seed mean 99.64\%$\pm$0.49 (seeds 42/123/456: 99.92/99.08/99.92). \texttt{exception\_only}: 99.83\%$\pm$0.00 (3 seeds). $^\S$VOTA: 3-seed mean 99.05\%$\pm$0.38 (99.41/98.66/99.08). $^\ddag$\texttt{loop\_only}: 3-seed mean 86.05\%$\pm$0.52 (85.63/85.88/86.64). Seed variance negatively correlates with information density: $\sigma{=}$0.00 (exception) ${<}$ 0.38 (VOTA) ${<}$ 0.49 (ae) ${<}$ 0.52 (loop).}
\label{tab:ablation}
\small
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Components} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{Tier} \\
\midrule
ae\_only & assertion-point & 99.64$^\dag$ & [99.26, 99.87] & 1 \\
exception\_only & exception events & \textbf{99.83} & [99.58, 100.00] & 1 \\
VOTA & exc+ae+loop & 99.05$^\S$ & [98.49, 99.50] & --- \\
VOTA\_no\_ae & exc+loop & 99.41 & [98.90, 99.80] & --- \\
loop\_only & loop compression & 86.05$^\ddag$ & [83.97, 87.96] & 2 \\
full\_trace & complete trace & 81.76 & [79.70, 83.90] & --- \\
no\_trace & none & 75.13 & [72.77, 77.48] & --- \\
\midrule
Regex (best) & exc.\ type regex & 93.61 & --- & --- \\
3-shot (Qwen-7B) & in-context learning & 90.84 & --- & --- \\
Zero-shot (4 models) & prompting & 51.0--93.5 & --- & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}%
}
\end{table}

Tier~1 signals are individually sufficient: \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%$\pm$0.00) exceeds VOTA (99.05\%$\pm$0.38) by +0.78pp (2/3 seeds $p{<}0.05$, all directionally consistent), implying that combining signals introduces noise.
Removing assertion points has no effect (\texttt{VOTA\_no\_ae} = 99.41\%, single seed), confirming exception dominance.
Tier~2 \texttt{loop\_only} lifts over \texttt{no\_trace} are model-dependent: Qwen-7B +10.92pp (86.05\%, $p{<}0.0001$), DeepSeek +7.90pp (81.26\%, CI [79.08, 83.45]), CodeLlama +0.59pp (77.06\%, n.s.).
\paragraph{Rule-based baseline comparison.}
The strongest non-trivial regex heuristic (B4: exception class name matching; Table~\ref{tab:regex}) achieves 93.61\% accuracy (F1=0.876), trailing SFT \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%, F1=0.997) by 6.22pp (McNemar $p{<}0.001$).
The gap concentrates on caught-exception boundary cases: regex flags all exception events as failures, while SFT learns to distinguish caught exceptions (benign, inside \texttt{try/except}) from uncaught faults, correctly resolving 6/8 boundary samples (Appendix~\ref{sec:regex_baselines}).
Across trace formats, SFT consistently outperforms the best applicable regex, from +3.62pp (\texttt{no\_trace} over majority baseline) to +23.86pp (VOTA), with the largest gains on formats requiring semantic interpretation (Appendix~\ref{sec:regex_baselines}).

\paragraph{Zero-shot and few-shot LLM baselines.}
Zero-shot prompting spans 51.0--93.5\% across four models (42.44pp range), with performance uncorrelated with model size (Qwen-1.5B: 93.45\% vs.\ CodeLlama-13B: 51.01\%).
Three-shot ICL on Qwen-7B (90.84\%) improves only 1.76pp and still trails SFT by 8.99pp.
SFT compresses this 42.44pp range to 0.56pp (99.33--99.89\%), closing a 6--49pp gap with 4,720 training samples (Appendix~\ref{sec:zeroshot_cross_model}).

\subsection{Format Marker Ablation}
\label{sec:nomarker}

The \texttt{exception\_only} format includes a \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} marker in all pass-class samples (regex baseline B5 exploits this for 99.33\% accuracy; Appendix~\ref{sec:regex_baselines}).
To quantify the marker's contribution, we retrain with all format markers removed (\texttt{nomarker} condition).

Qwen-7B 3-seed mean: 97.65\% $\pm$ 0.96 (seeds 42/123/456: 96.55/98.32/98.07\%), a drop of 2.18pp from \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%).
Qwen-1.5B: 97.82\%, drop of 2.01pp.
The marker contribution (${\sim}$2pp) accounts for only ${\sim}$9\% of the total exception lift over \texttt{no\_trace} (24.70pp on 7B).
Exception events thus provide two signal layers that show no degradation at smaller scale: structural markers (${\sim}$2pp, regex-learnable) and semantic exception content (${\sim}$22pp, requiring SFT to distinguish caught from uncaught exceptions).

\subsection{Information Density Decomposition}
\label{sec:density}

The 17.29pp gap between \texttt{full\_trace} (81.76\%) and VOTA (99.05\%, 3-seed mean) decomposes via \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only} (85.94\%$\pm$1.12, 3 seeds; Table~\ref{tab:density}), which retains the full trace but masks all trace tokens from the loss.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Approximate information density decomposition: gradient dilution (${\sim}$24\%) vs.\ information overload (${\sim}$76\%). \texttt{label\_only} and VOTA are 3-seed means on Qwen-7B.}
\label{tab:density}
\small
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{$\Delta$ vs.\ full\_trace} & \textbf{Gap explained} \\
\midrule
full\_trace & 81.76 & --- & --- \\
label\_only & 85.94{\scriptsize$\pm$1.12} & +4.18pp & 24\% \\
VOTA & 99.05{\scriptsize$\pm$0.38} & +17.29pp & 100\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}%
}
\end{table}

Gradient dilution accounts for approximately 24\% of the gap (+4.18pp, 3-seed mean): when the model no longer wastes gradient updates on predicting trace tokens, accuracy improves even with identical input.
The remaining ${\sim}$76\% (+13.11pp) reflects information overload at inference: the model receives thousands of irrelevant trace lines that compete for attention with the diagnostic signal, regardless of loss design.
This asymmetry implies that trace compression methods should prioritize \emph{content selection} (removing irrelevant lines) over \emph{loss engineering} (masking non-target tokens), as the larger bottleneck is what the model sees, not how it is trained.
The two factors may interact, so this decomposition is approximate.
Label-only loss simultaneously changes multiple optimization dynamics (effective gradient norm, implicit regularization from trace token prediction); the 24\%/76\% attribution should be interpreted as an approximate decomposition rather than a strict causal partition.
This analysis uses 3 seeds on a single model (Qwen-7B); cross-model validation remains future work.

\subsection{Additional Analyses}
\label{sec:additional}

\paragraph{Trace length ablation.}
\label{sec:trace_length}
Varying the head-truncated trace token budget (256--no limit) on Qwen-7B yields accuracy in a narrow 77.2\%--81.8\% band with a non-monotonic pattern: 1024-token prefixes (77.23\%) underperform 512-token prefixes (80.42\%, $p{=}0.002$), because mid-length prefixes retain enough irrelevant content to mislead the model while discarding diagnostic events near the trace terminus (Appendix~\ref{sec:trace_length_full}).
This non-monotonicity is specific to head-truncation; under tail-truncation, accuracy increases monotonically for two of three models (Table~\ref{tab:tail_cross_model} in Appendix), with only DeepSeek showing a mild architecture-specific reversal at tail-1024$\to$tail-2048 ($-$1.5pp).

\paragraph{Truncation direction and budget curve.}
Tail-truncation (retaining the last $k$ tokens) dramatically outperforms head-truncation: among the three models with complete data, tail-2048 exceeds head-2048 by 15.5--22.6pp, with the gap widening at smaller scale (Qwen-1.5B: +22.6pp vs.\ Qwen-7B: +15.5pp; Appendix~\ref{sec:trace_length_full}, Table~\ref{tab:head_vs_tail}).
All four models' head-2048 accuracies converge into a narrow 75.3--81.8\% band (6.5pp), comparable to the tail-256 band (72.6--78.9\%, 6.3pp), indicating that signal-poor conditions produce a shared performance floor regardless of scale or architecture.

A cross-model budget sweep across four models and three architecture families reveals a phase transition localized between 384 and 512 tail tokens.
At tail-384, all models remain near baseline (73.6--82.9\%, only +1.0--6.5pp over tail-256); the steep jump occurs at 384$\to$512 (+11.0--22.0pp), crossing from near-baseline to near-ceiling (${\sim}$94--98\%).
This localizes the critical threshold to ${\sim}$400--500 tokens, matching the typical exception traceback length (Table~\ref{tab:tail_cross_model}).
Beyond 512 tokens, accuracy converges further: multi-seed validation across all 12 model$\times$seed combinations confirms all tail-512 accuracies fall within a 4.63pp band [93.61\%, 98.24\%] (Table~\ref{tab:tail512_seeds}); at tail-1024, three models reach 96.5--98.2\%, compressing the 6.3pp cross-model spread observed at tail-256.
\texttt{tail\_2048} captures 95--98\% of \texttt{exception\_only}'s accuracy across all completed configurations.
The residual 2--5pp gap confirms that semantic extraction (identifying exception type and message) still outperforms positional extraction (retaining a fixed window containing non-diagnostic lines).

\paragraph{Calibration.}
\label{sec:calibration}
Calibration mirrors the tier hierarchy: \texttt{exception\_only} achieves ECE = 0.0027 vs.\ 0.171 for \texttt{no\_trace}, a 63$\times$ gap (Figure~\ref{fig:calibration}).
This calibration advantage generalizes across architectures and scales: all four models (1.5B--13B) achieve ECE ${<}$ 0.007 under \texttt{exception\_only} (Appendix~\ref{sec:calibration_full}).

\paragraph{Error orthogonality.}
\texttt{exception\_only}'s 2 errors have zero overlap with all other conditions' error sets (Jaccard = 0.000), confirming it operates on an independent signal dimension (Appendix~\ref{sec:error_overlap}).

\paragraph{Exception type breakdown.}
A per-exception-type breakdown (Appendix~\ref{sec:exception_type}) confirms that all standard exception types achieve 100\% accuracy; the only failures arise from \texttt{GeneratorExit}, a benign \texttt{BaseException} subclass.

\paragraph{Cross-dataset generalization.}
\label{sec:debugbench}
On DebugBench \citep{tian2024debugbench} ($N{=}426$), the ranking is preserved: \texttt{exception\_only} 100\%, VOTA 99.77\%, \texttt{no\_trace} 96.71\%; narrow margins reflect a ceiling effect from structurally distinctive mutations (Appendix~\ref{sec:debugbench_full}).

1	\section{Method}
2	
3	\subsection{Task Definition}
4	
5	We study \emph{verdict prediction}: given a Python function, a test input, and an optional execution trace, predict whether the test passes or fails.
6	The model produces a single token (\texttt{pass} or \texttt{fail}), making this a binary classification task.
7	Unlike code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile} or output prediction \citep{gu2024cruxeval}, verdict prediction isolates the model's ability to detect faults from its ability to simulate execution.
8	The discrete binary outcome makes the effect of each trace component directly measurable, providing cleaner ablation contrasts than generation tasks where output quality varies continuously.
9	
10	\subsection{Dataset}
11	\label{sec:dataset}
12	
13	We sampled 10 candidate solutions per problem from Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (temperature 0.8, top\_p 0.95) for 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} (164) and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program} (427), executed each against canonical tests with \texttt{sys.settrace} to obtain line-level traces and pass/fail verdicts, yielding 5,910 pairs (67\% pass, 33\% fail).
14	The dataset is split 80/20 by problem ID into 4,720 training and 1,190 test samples (majority baseline: 71.51\%).
15	The \texttt{exception\_only} format collapses passing solutions into identical rows (39.45\% train, 48.99\% test duplicates); these duplicates arise from multiple candidate solutions per problem, with the train--test split enforced at the problem level (472 train / 119 test problems, zero crossover; Appendix~\ref{sec:dedup_stats}).
16	
17	\subsection{Trace Representations}
18	
19	We define seven conditions that vary the trace information available (Figure~\ref{fig:trace_overview}):
20	\begin{itemize}
21	\item \texttt{no\_trace}: Source code and test input only.
22	\item \texttt{full\_trace}: Complete line-by-line trace with variable states.
23	\item \texttt{VOTA}: Exception events + assertion-point comparisons + loop compression (Appendix~\ref{sec:vota_algorithm}).
24	\item \texttt{exception\_only}: Only exception/error events.
25	\item \texttt{ae\_only}: Only assertion-point actual/expected pairs.
26	\item \texttt{loop\_only}: Only loop compression summaries.
27	\item \texttt{VOTA\_no\_ae}: VOTA without assertion-point information.
28	\end{itemize}
29	
30	\begin{figure*}[t]
31	\centering
32	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_trace_overview}
33	\caption{Overview of the verdict prediction pipeline. Source code and a test input are executed to produce a full raw trace. Four conditions vary the trace information: \texttt{no\_trace} (75.13\%), \texttt{full\_trace} (81.76\%), VOTA (99.41\%), and \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%). Accuracies for Qwen-2.5-7B (seed=42, $N{=}1{,}190$). Appendix~\ref{sec:vota_examples} provides input/output examples.}
34	\label{fig:trace_overview}
35	\end{figure*}
36	
37	\subsection{Models and Training}
38	
39	We evaluate four models spanning three architecture families: \textbf{Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B-Instruct} \citep{qwen2025coder}, \textbf{CodeLlama-13B-Instruct} \citep{roziere2024code}, and \textbf{DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct} \citep{deepseek2024coder}, covering a 1.5B--13B parameter range (8.7$\times$).
40	All conditions use LoRA \citep{hu2022lora} (rank=16, $\alpha$=32, dropout=0.05) on all linear layers, 3 epochs, effective batch size 32, LR $2 \times 10^{-4}$ with linear warmup/decay, max sequence length 2{,}048 tokens.
41	Sequences exceeding this limit are truncated while preserving the verdict label.
42	The primary seed is 42; seeds 123 and 456 test \texttt{exception\_only} robustness (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_details}).
43	
44	\subsection{Loss Ablation}
45	
46	To disentangle training signal from input signal quality, we introduce \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only}: identical full-trace input but loss computed only on the verdict token (trace positions masked).
47	Improvement over standard \texttt{full\_trace} is attributable to \emph{gradient dilution}; the remaining gap to VOTA reflects \emph{information overload} at inference time.
